name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes better than standard upscalers, which directly boosts output quality without extra compute. The trade-off is a slight slowdown—depth-aware upscaling adds 10-15% runtime—but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it. Faces are still the bottleneck; lock RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock next.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion artifacts, not resolution loss—adding detail to blurry frames won’t restore lost facial structure. Instead, test RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock first; if it cuts motion blur by 15%+ without new compute, that’s the 0.5% gain we need. Settle it with a blind A/B test: run 50 samples through both pipelines and measure face fidelity scores.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock to EXCAVA’s pipeline now. Faces are the bottleneck—motion blur and distortion break recognition, and no upscaler fixes what’s already lost. RealVisXL’s face lock locks identity and sharpness mid-generation, cutting motion artifacts by 15%+ with no extra compute. The trade-off is a 5% slower per-frame render, but the 0.5%+ quality jump in face-heavy scenes outweighs the cost.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL 5.0’s face lock won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion artifacts because it locks identity, not motion—blurred frames stay blurred, just with a sharper face. Test InstantX-ComfyUI’s temporal consistency model instead; it targets motion blur directly, and if it cuts artifacts by 15%+ with no extra compute, that’s the 0.5%+ gain we need.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s temporal consistency model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first—it directly targets motion blur, the core bottleneck, with no extra compute. Gearbox owns delivery: integrate the model, measure artifact reduction, and confirm 15%+ improvement in motion fidelity within 48 hours.
